question: How does Pydantic work for data validation in FastAPI and what are the common patterns?
title: Pydantic Models and Validation
direct_answer: Pydantic models are Python classes with type-annotated fields. Pydantic validates and coerces data on instantiation — if you pass '42' for an int field, Pydantic converts it. Invalid data raises ValidationError. In FastAPI, Pydantic models define request bodies, response shapes, and query param bundles. Field() adds constraints (min_length, regex, ge, le). Validators (@field_validator) add custom logic. Use separate Create/Update/Response schemas — never reuse one model for all operations.
interviewer_intent: Tests Pydantic fluency — it's the validation layer in every FastAPI project and increasingly used standalone in other frameworks.

sections.title: Pydantic validation patterns
sections.content:
Pydantic v2 (current) uses __annotations__ and runs validation at instantiation time. Key behaviors:

Coercion: by default, Pydantic coerces compatible types. String '42' becomes int 42. model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True) disables coercion.

Field(): annotate with extra constraints. Field(min_length=3) for strings. Field(ge=0, le=100) for numbers. Field(default=None) for optional fields. Field(alias='user_id') for JSON keys that differ from Python attribute names.

@field_validator: custom validation. @model_validator: cross-field validation (password == confirm_password). Validators raise ValueError on failure.

Schema separation: Create (input, no id), Response (output, include id, exclude sensitive fields), Update (all fields optional for PATCH). This prevents callers from setting read-only fields like id or created_at.

From ORM: model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) enables UserResponse.model_validate(db_user) — reads SQLAlchemy model attributes directly.

sections.title: Pydantic patterns
Pydantic rules
items: Separate Create, Update, Response schemas — don't reuse one schema
ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) for ORM object → Pydantic model

seo.metaTitle: Pydantic Models and Validation — FastAPI Best Practices
seo.metaDescription: Master Pydantic for FastAPI: separate Create/Update/Response schemas, Field constraints, @field_validator, @model_validator, and from_attributes for ORM objects.

speakable_v2.hook: Pydantic's rule: one schema shape for one use case. Never share the Create schema with the Response schema — one has a password field, the other definitely should not.

beats.content: Use separate schemas: Create (input, includes password), Update (all fields optional for PATCH), Response (output, no sensitive fields, includes id and timestamps). This prevents callers from setting read-only server-managed fields.

Field() adds constraints that are validated on every instantiation. Field(min_length=3) for strings, Field(ge=0) for 'greater than or equal to zero'. FastAPI turns ValidationError into a 422 response automatically.
@field_validator for single-field custom logic. @model_validator for cross-field checks like password confirmation or date ranges.

speakable_v2.cap: from_attributes=True (ConfigDict) lets you pass SQLAlchemy ORM objects directly to Pydantic model_validate() — it reads attributes by name. Without it, you'd have to convert to a dict manually.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Pydantic v2 strict mode, or handling partial updates with Optional fields in PATCH endpoints.
